title: Hazel and the Harbor
premise: In 1917, Juniper Lockridge keeps a secret ledger of wounded soldiers' names that army officers have struck from official records, believing the omissions hide a requisition scheme that will strip the harbor town of Hazel Bay of its homes and ships. When the army seizes the town and orders all documents burned, Juniper and the found family of dockworkers, fishermen, and fellow nurses who shelter her must smuggle the ledger past three military checkpoints to a naval inquiry in the city. Betrayed by the town's own magistrate, they lose two of their own before Juniper chooses to testify rather than flee, exposing the corruption at cost of her commission. The book ends with the inquiry vindicating the names in the ledger, Hazel Bay's people rebuilding together, and Juniper finally understanding that belonging is not something carried, but something built.
about_author: Rosalind Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime correspondence in coastal county records. She writes historical fiction about the people history forgot to list.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Juniper, a battlefield nurse stationed near Hazel Bay, records in her private ledger the names of soldiers erased from official rolls after a disastrous convoy. Her colleague Maren notices and asks why she keeps count. POV: Juniper. Beat: quiet resolve; establishes Juniper's belief that a name is the one thing that can't be requisitioned.

chapters.title: Orders Come to Hazel Bay
chapters.summary: The army requisitions Hazel Bay: homes seized, fishing boats impressed, and all town documents ordered surrendered for burning. Juniper watches the magistrate, Aldous Crane, welcome the officers with suspicious warmth. POV: Juniper. Beat: dread and displacement; the town's rhythm shatters and the ledger becomes contraband.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Kept
chapters.summary: Juniper hides the ledger inside a fishmonger's ice crate with the help of dockworker Silas Penn and his orphaned niece Tilly, her found family forming in earnest. They learn the erased names match men pressed into a secret salvage operation. POV: Silas. Beat: tentative solidarity; strangers become conspirators over salted fish and shared grief.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: A naval inquiry in the city will hear testimony in nine days, but the road passes three military checkpoints. The group maps the route: the causeway, the ferry yard, the garrison bridge. Maren volunteers as courier, believing her uniform will protect her. POV: Maren. Beat: rising stakes; hope sharpened into a plan with a deadline.

chapters.title: The Causeway at Low Tide
chapters.summary: First attempt: Tilly carries the ledger through the causeway checkpoint hidden in a mourning wreath for her father. A suspicious corporal delays her, and only a fisherman's staged quarrel buys her passage. POV: Tilly. Beat: fear and small triumph; the child proves braver than the adults expected.

chapters.title: Crane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Magistrate Crane discovers the ledger exists and offers Juniper immunity in exchange for handing it over, revealing he profits from the requisition. She refuses; he threatens to name her accomplices. POV: Juniper. Beat: corruption's face-to-face seduction; Juniper understands the cost has a name now, and it's everyone she loves.

chapters.title: The Ferry Yard
chapters.summary: Second checkpoint: Maren crosses with a decoy ledger while Silas rows the real one across the estuary at night. The decoy is discovered; Maren is arrested and the garrison tightens every crossing. POV: Silas. Beat: sacrifice and guilt; the plan holds but the family pays in flesh.

chapters.title: What Cannot Be Carried
chapters.summary: With the garrison bridge impassable and Maren imprisoned, the group fractures—some urge Juniper to burn the ledger and flee by sea. She refuses: the names are the point. They plan to walk the ledger through the last checkpoint in plain sight, hidden in a coffin bound for burial. POV: Juniper. Beat: darkest hour and the turn; despair transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: The Garrison Bridge
chapters.summary: Climax: the town turns out for a staged funeral, dozens of mourners shielding the coffin as Crane himself inspects it at the bridge. Juniper steps forward, reveals her identity, and demands he search it before his own officers—forcing him to wave it through to protect his scheme. POV: Juniper. Beat: white-knuckle climax; the whole town becomes the ledger's cover.

chapters.title: Read Into the Record
chapters.summary: At the inquiry, Juniper testifies and reads the names aloud, one by one, as Crane's accounts unravel; Maren is released and the salvage operation exposed. Hazel Bay's requisition is reversed, and the town rebuilds around a harbor memorial carved with every name. POV: Juniper. Beat: resolution and belonging; Juniper stops measuring what can be carried and stays to build what remains.
